name: Glass hair
image_alt: A woman in profile with a smooth, glossy braided low bun and defined edges, blowing a pink bubble.
tagline: Two wash days to the glossiest your coils can get.
description: A simple two-wash plan for glossy coils: wash one clarifies and preps, wash two glosses.
intro: Shine comes from a smooth surface, so the plan is simple: clear off what's dulling your hair, then add the gloss. Two wash days, one job each. The aim is the glossiest your coils can get, with healthy hair as the part that does not move.

stock.title: Before you start
stock.intro: Two minutes now makes the result easy to see later.
items: Same spot and same light each time. Indoor light hides shine.
Hair looks dull and feels rough even when it's clean? Hard water may be the reason. Wash one has a step for it.
Colour, bleach, relaxer, regular heat? Some gloss treatments are acidic, so follow each label.

routine.title: The how-to
routine.intro: Do wash one first. Do wash two a week or so later, or when your next wash day comes round.

washes.title: Wash one: clear and prep
steps: Shampoo with a clarifying shampoo to lift product buildup and oils. Gloss can't work through a film of old product. Section your hair first and keep it detangled.
Chelate, if your water is hard
Hard water leaves minerals on hair that clarifying shampoos don't always remove. A chelating shampoo targets them. Some products do both jobs, so you may not need two.
Deep condition so the strand is soft and flexible before any gloss goes on. Detangle while the conditioner is in.
Pick one from the list and follow its label for timing. Rinse well.

steps.label: Glossing masks, pick one
use: JVN Revive Rapid Repair Bond Gloss
Gisou Honey Gloss Ceramide Therapy Mask

steps: Leave-in on soaking wet hair, then your usual gel or cream, smoothed through each section. Let the coils clump and leave them alone while they dry.

washes.title: Wash two: gloss
steps: Cleanse the scalp and let the lather rinse down the lengths. Nothing harsh today, you're about to add shine.
Gloss, with a mask and/or a hair gloss

Use a glossing mask, a hair gloss, or one after the other if the labels say that's fine. Start with just one product the first time so you know what's working. Do not stack several glosses on one wash day.

steps.label: Glosses, pick one to start
use: JVN Revive Rapid Repair Bond Gloss
Gisou Honey Gloss Ceramide Therapy Mask

steps: Same as wash one. Clump, smooth and leave your coils alone while they dry. A clumped coil gives one long highlight, while a cloud of separate strands gives lots of tiny ones.
One or two drops of serum or light oil on the outside and the ends. This is the actual polish, and the easiest step to overdo. Satin at night.

between.title: Keeping it glossy
groups: Check the ends, not the roots. If they feel soft, do nothing at all.
A light mist of water and a little leave-in on dry parts only.
Satin bonnet or pillowcase and loose twists. Nothing tight.

trouble.title: If something feels off
items: That's buildup. Clarify again, and add products back one at a time.
Think hard water. Try the chelating step.
Shiny on day one, dull by day three
Look at nights first: satin, loose styles, ends tucked. Then at how much you touch it.
Too much oil, or oil on hair that wasn't fully dry. One or two drops, on the outside only.
Check that you clarified first, and compare in daylight against your own photo, not someone else's hair.

end.title: After your two washes
notes: Put your photo from after wash two next to the one you took today. That comparison is the only honest answer to whether it worked.
Keep the clarify step whenever hair feels coated, and keep the gloss at whatever pace you enjoy.
